title: Bound BIT sender fusion at owned recipients (0% κ change)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

NO VERIFIED GAIN. The strongest independently reproduced comparable κ remains 0.003644407895539 (#7156, head b44944c3058d522cbff17836e16240d40d77a927). The exact change is 0 (0%). This package proves a scoped exclusion for changing the retained #7001 BIT word at fixed owned-receiver contracts.

The replay checks all 360 one-intervening-ADD sends, granting the full sender gap and every recipient read barrier. All 120 receiver groups lack a common early chart. The late chart either lacks the retained consumer or charges a summary descent that outweighs three optimistic fusions. An independent row-span formulation excludes all 840 single, double, and triple alias subsets even with arbitrary combinations of retained rank-seven rows in the original lifetimes.

## Task and overlap

Base e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57. Exact source heads, paths and hashes are in [SOURCES.json](https://github.com/ToikY/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a3352606f71a97ab3a707ee6c5173df6345c5f38/research/bit-send-cochart-gate/SOURCES.json). The sender scope refines the BIT moonshot investigation in #7111. #7157 supplies a distinct earlier-carrier gate. Its proof does not cover the recipient cochart, grouped sender, or alias tests here.

## Validation

From a clean checkout with CPython 3.12 (tested 3.12.14):

~~~sh
python3.12 -I -B research/bit-send-cochart-gate/verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-send-cochart-gate
python3.12 scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/bit-send-cochart-gate --check-modes
~~~

The standalone replay checks 659 final rows and 840 restore-original positive controls. A modified source byte is rejected. The proof charges the late descent with an analytic inequality. No physical rewrite survives the finite gates, so candidate native/compiler verification does not apply. Local metadata, registered replay, and committed-byte checks passed.

## Credit

Ali Romman’s retained BIT provider (#5421), the #6834/#7001 word and its authors, and #7149/#7157’s carrier methodology supply the predecessor construction and tests. #7156 supplies the current complete comparison. OpenAI Codex and subagents materially assisted the proofs, verifier and independent replay.

## Open next question

Test coupled paid arrivals on asynchronous role clocks with exact original row restoration. Changed consumer routes and changed caller interfaces remain open.
